slides.title: Have you ever...?
slides.body: Think of something amazing you did!
slides.notes: Show the picture. Elicit: 'Have you ever eaten something strange?' (2 min). ICQ: Are you thinking or writing?

slides.title: Present Perfect — Form
slides.notes: Write on board: I have visited. She has eaten. They have seen. Drill pronunciation of participles. (3 min)

slides.title: Ever and Never
slides.body:
Ever = in your life?
Never = not in my life
slides.notes: Example: 'Have you ever been to the beach?' 'I have never been to the beach.' Elicit more examples. (3 min)

slides.title: Affirmative
slides.notes: Show affirmative. Point out: have + past participle 'seen'. (1 min)

slides.title: Negative
slides.notes: Point out: NOT goes between have and past participle. (1 min)

slides.title: Question
slides.notes: Point out: HAVE moves to the start. (1 min)

slides.title: Choose the correct form
slides.notes: Show fragment first (blank), next click reveals answer 'has'. Wait 5 seconds between clicks. (2 min). ICQ: Are you writing or just looking?

slides.body:
Unscramble the sentence

you ever have eaten sushi?

Unscramble the sentence

Have you ever eaten sushi?
slides.notes: Students write the correct order. Then the words fly into place. (2 min)

slides.title: Ask your partner!
slides.body:
Have you ever eaten Thai food?
Have you ever gone to the beach?
Have you ever seen a ghost?
slides.notes: Pair work. Student A asks, Student B answers 'Yes, I have / No, I haven't.' (4 min). Monitor and take notes for error correction.

slides.title: Report your partner
slides.body:
She has eaten Thai food.
He has never gone to the beach.
slides.notes: Students report to class: 'She has eaten Thai food.' 'He has never gone to the beach.' (3 min). Expected: have/has + past participle.

slides.title: Two Truths, One Lie
slides.body:
Write three things you have done.
One is not true.
Your partner guesses the lie!
slides.notes: Example: 'I have climbed a mountain. I have eaten snake. I have flown a plane.' Partners guess the lie. (5 min)

slides.title: Great job today!
slides.body: Now I can talk about my experiences!
slides.notes: Exit ticket: 'What is one thing you have done that you are proud of?' (2 min). Next class: Present Perfect with 'just, already, yet'.
